classification.difficultyReason: Represent opposite and reciprocal roots symbolically, simplify the coefficient relationships and substitute to prove two identities.

content.prompt: The polynomial $P(x)=x^4+ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$ has two zeroes that are opposites and two zeroes that are reciprocals. Show that $b=1+d$ and $c=ad$.

answer.worked:
Let the roots be $\alpha,-\alpha,\beta,\dfrac1\beta$, where $\beta\ne0$.

Sum of roots:
$$\beta+\frac1\beta=-a\qquad(1)$$
Sum of products two at a time:
$$\begin{align*}-\alpha^2+\alpha\beta+\frac\alpha\beta-\alpha\beta-\frac\alpha\beta+1&=b\\-\alpha^2+1&=b\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Sum of products three at a time:
$$\begin{align*}-\alpha^2\beta-\frac{\alpha^2}{\beta}+\alpha-\alpha&=-c\\-\alpha^2\left(\beta+\frac1\beta\right)&=-c\qquad(3)\end{align*}$$
Product of roots:
$$-\alpha^2=d\qquad(4)$$
Substitute (4) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}d+1&=b\\b&=1+d.\end{align*}$$
Substitute (1) and (4) into (3):
$$\begin{align*}d(-a)&=-c\\-ad&=-c\\c&=ad.\end{align*}$$
